correctness.rationale: For the unit-edge vertex metric on K_1 joined to m>=2 disjoint cliques (N>=m+2 peripheral vertices), reconstructing the hub zero-sum coefficient gives exactly Q_p=-sum_{peripheral}z_v^2+(1-2^p)sum_i s_i^2+(2^p-2)(sum_i s_i)^2. Within-blade and weighted Cauchy-Schwarz are simultaneously sharp, yielding necessary-and-sufficient (q-2)sum k_i/(1+(q-1)k_i)<=1. The left side increases from zero to m, so its unique root q>2 sets critical p=log_2 q. Cauchy-Schwarz equality gives one-dimensional null space at criticality; Schoenberg centering gives minimal Euclidean snowflake embedding dimension N-1 at critical and N below. Strict concavity of h_q(k)=k/(1+(q-1)k), combined with integer Robin-Hood transfers, proves strict root increase under non-permutation majorization and the unique balanced/unbalanced fixed-budget extrema. Independently calculated full zero-sum distance-powered matrix eigenvalues for k=(2,2,2),(1,2,3),(1,1,4),(1,3),(2,2), checking critical zero and negative other eigenvalues; finite tests only corroborate the universal proof.
